title: Neonatal & Pediatric Respiratory Care Mock Exam

questions.text: A term newborn is in respiratory distress, and a chest x-ray reveals bowel, stomach, and part of the liver in the thoracic cavity with one severely compromised lung. What is the diagnosis and initial management?

answers.text: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia — remove bowel gas, slowly suction the abdominal contents back to position, and close the breach
Gastroschisis — cover the exposed intestines and begin antibiotics
Tension pneumothorax — perform immediate needle decompression
Meconium aspiration syndrome — intubate and suction the ETT until clear

questions.text: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is most common in premature infants because they have:

answers.text: Low blood flow to the intestines and underdeveloped intestinal tracts, which — with early gut bacteria — can infect and kill the intestinal wall
A CFTR mutation that thickens intestinal secretions and obstructs the bowel
An abdominal wall defect that exposes the intestines to outside infection
Excess swallowed surfactant that irritates and inflames the gut lining

questions.text: In utero, the ductus arteriosus shunts blood away from the lungs because:

answers.text: Pulmonary vascular pressure is higher than systemic vascular pressure
Systemic vascular pressure is higher than pulmonary vascular pressure
The lungs are fully oxygenating fetal blood
Prostaglandin levels are low before birth

questions.text: Which shunt closes rapidly after birth, aided by clamping the umbilical cord?
A mother is over 35 years old. Based on maternal risk factors, her infant is at increased risk for:

answers.text: Prematurity and chromosomal defects such as Down syndrome
Low birth weight and facial dysmorphology

questions.text: The placenta is best described as:

answers.text: The organ of respiration for the fetus, extracting O₂ and excreting CO₂
A passive filter that only removes waste
The structure that produces fetal surfactant
A shunt between the liver and the inferior vena cava

questions.text: An L/S ratio of 2:1 from amniocentesis indicates:

answers.text: Stable surfactant production in a mature lung

questions.text: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) in an infant is the regurgitation of stomach contents. Which respiratory complications can it lead to?

answers.text: Reactive airway disease, pneumonia, and other upper-airway issues
Retinopathy of prematurity and intraventricular hemorrhage
Surfactant deficiency and hyaline membrane formation
Subglottic stenosis and a steeple sign on neck x-ray

questions.text: Which two groups of newborns are most likely to need intervention at delivery?

answers.text: Infants with evidence of meconium and premature infants
Infants delivered vaginally and large-for-gestational-age infants
Term infants with normal APGAR scores
Infants of mothers without risk factors

questions.text: A premature infant (30 weeks) requires resuscitation. What starting FiO₂ is recommended?
During resuscitation, the heart rate remains below 60/min after 30 seconds of effective PPV. The next step is to:
The Ballard Maturational Assessment is used to determine:

answers.text: Gestational age, using six physical and neurological signs
The severity of lung disease after birth

questions.text: An infant weighs 900 grams at birth. This is classified as:
The Silverman scoring system identifies the severity of lung disease using observable signs because:

answers.text: Auscultation of the infant chest is difficult due to size and sound transfer
Infants cannot be placed on pulse oximetry
Blood gases are never available in neonates
Chest x-rays are contraindicated in infants

questions.text: A chest x-ray showing diffuse reticulogranular (ground glass) densities, air bronchograms, and low lung volumes is most characteristic of:
Surfactant produced before 34–35 weeks is ineffective at lowering surface tension because:

answers.text: It is trapped inside the alveolar type II cells and cannot be released
It is destroyed by fetal hemoglobin
It is washed out by retained lung fluid
It is not produced until 36 weeks

questions.text: Which surfactant preparation is correctly matched to its generic name?
Recommended saturation and PaO₂ targets for a pre-term infant are:
Head bobbing, chin up, and abdominal expansion in a pediatric patient are signs of:
RDS is also known as:

answers.text: Hyaline membrane disease, a lung disease of prematurity
Type II RDS, the most common newborn disorder

questions.text: Transient tachypnea of the newborn is most associated with:

answers.text: Slow clearance of lung fluid, especially after cesarean section; resolves in 24–48 hours
Inhalation of meconium in a term infant

questions.text: Treatment options for apnea of prematurity include:
In PPHN, blood continues to shunt through the foramen ovale and ductus arteriosus after birth because:

answers.text: Pulmonary vascular resistance rises above systemic vascular resistance
Systemic vascular resistance rises above pulmonary vascular resistance
The placenta continues to function after delivery

questions.text: From an RT standpoint, the two most important contributors to BPD are:
Correct management of a severely depressed term infant with meconium streaking is:

answers.text: Intubate and apply direct ETT suction (−70 to −100 mmHg) until clear or after 2–4 aspirations
Aggressive bag-mask ventilation to push the meconium through

questions.text: To reduce the likelihood of retinopathy of prematurity, maintain:

answers.text: PaO₂ less than 80 mmHg, with SpO₂ between >88% and <94%

questions.text: A ventilated preterm infant develops PIE. The most appropriate ventilator response is to:

answers.text: Lower airway pressures, ideally by switching to high-frequency jet ventilation
Increase PEEP and PIP to recruit collapsed lung

questions.text: A congenital defect where the intestines are found outside the body, exiting beside the umbilicus, is:
The single most important guidance to reduce SIDS risk is to:

answers.text: Place the infant supine or side-lying and remove excess blankets and toys
Place the infant prone with extra blankets
Keep the room cold during winter

questions.text: Bronchiolitis is usually caused by:
A child with stridor, a barking seal cough, and a steeple sign on A-P neck x-ray most likely has:
Epiglottitis differs from croup in that it is:

answers.text: Supraglottic swelling with a thumb sign on lateral neck x-ray, most often from H. influenzae
Subglottic swelling with a steeple sign, most often from parainfluenza
A lower respiratory tract infection from RSV
Always managed safely with repeated airway exams

questions.text: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a mutation affecting:

answers.text: The CFTR protein that regulates chloride ion movement across cell membranes
Surfactant production by type II cells

questions.text: CPAP (NCPAP) is indicated, rather than contraindicated, in which scenario?

answers.text: PaO₂ < 50 mmHg or an FiO₂ requirement > 60% with adequate spontaneous effort
Respiratory arrest with no spontaneous effort

questions.text: The respiratory time constant is calculated as:
A stiff, surfactant-deficient neonatal lung has a short time constant, which means:

answers.text: The lungs fill and empty faster, so shorter I:E ratios are needed
The lungs fill and empty slower, so longer I:E ratios are needed
Compliance is high and resistance is low
Inspiratory time should be set to 1 second

questions.text: On a neonatal ventilator, peak inspiratory pressure should generally not exceed:

answers.text: 30 cmH₂O, except for prematurity or chest-wall rigidity from fentanyl

questions.text: An appropriate tidal volume for a neonate with normal lung function is:
Which is an AARC indication to intubate an infant?

answers.text: Hypoxemia with PaO₂ < 50 mmHg, or hypercapnia with pH < 7.20–7.25
An SpO₂ of 95% on room air
A respiratory rate of 45 breaths/min in a neonate

questions.text: Air collecting within the chest but outside the normal air cells of the lungs describes:

answers.text: Air leak syndromes (e.g., pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, PIE)

questions.text: The primary goal of high-frequency ventilation is to:

answers.text: Provide adequate ventilation and oxygenation while limiting lung injury
Deliver large tidal volumes to maximize CO₂ removal
Avoid the need for any sedation
Eliminate the need for mean airway pressure

questions.text: On HFOV, which setting primarily controls CO₂ removal?
On HFOV, to eliminate MORE CO₂ you should:

answers.text: Decrease the frequency, allowing more time for pressure to reach the alveoli
Increase the frequency to deliver more cycles

questions.text: On HFOV, the MAP is titrated for lung recruitment until expansion reaches:
High-frequency jet ventilation is characterized by:

answers.text: High-velocity jets from a nozzle/injector with passive exhalation, used mostly for BPD, PIE, and air leaks
A piston that actively pushes and pulls gas, used for all adult patients
Active exhalation with a long inspiratory time
Tidal volumes larger than anatomic dead space

questions.text: On HFJV, a sudden DECREASE in servo pressure may indicate:

answers.text: Worsening compliance/resistance, an obstructed ETT, tension pneumothorax, or right mainstem intubation
A leak around the ETT as the baby grows
A tubing leak in the circuit

questions.text: A transcutaneous monitor differs from a pulse oximeter because it:

answers.text: Measures both PtcO₂ and PtcCO₂ and heats the skin to arterialize the capillaries
Measures oxygen saturation only, with higher accuracy

questions.text: Inhaled nitric oxide is best described as:

answers.text: A selective pulmonary vasodilator, started at 20 PPM, used for hypoxic respiratory failure/PPHN
A systemic vasoconstrictor that raises blood pressure
A bronchodilator that reduces airway resistance
A surfactant replacement delivered via the ETT

questions.text: Veno-arterial (VA) ECMO is distinguished from veno-venous (VV) ECMO because VA:

answers.text: Supports both the heart and the lungs
Uses only the right femoral vein

questions.text: Using Tube ID = (Age + 16) / 4, the estimated ETT internal diameter for an 8-year-old is:
